Active months are colored `theme.pageTextLight`; inactive ones are dimmed with `theme.pageTextSubdued`.

That's the **`MonthPicker`** component: [packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/MonthPicker.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/MonthPicker.tsx#L93-L110)

The calendar icon there (wrapped in a `Link` with `title={t('Today')}`) calls `onSelect(currentMonth)` on click, jumping the budget view back to the current month — that's the "top middle" icon you're seeing, distinct from the three `MonthCountSelector` icons in the top left. It sits alongside chevron-left/chevron-right buttons (`SvgCheveronLeft`/`SvgCheveronRight`, lines 111+) that page through months.

_**User (2026-09-11 00:47:14Z)**_

Let's update MonthCountSelector.tsx to make the UI appearance of MonthPicker.tsx. Specifically when hovering over the cursor should now change from a cursor to a hand and have a hover background effect. The logic and rough appearance of the MonthCountSelector.tsx component should remain unchanged, just making it more tacticle to fit the summary below.

In the budget section of the app where the monthly budgets are shown, the top left corner has multiple calendar icons to allow users to select how many months are displayed at a time. When you hover over most clickable icons on the app, the cursor changes from an arrow to a hand. Currently, the cursor does not change to a hand over these calendar icons. This makes it harder for the user to know that they can click on these, and it may prevent them from knowing that this functionality exists. Changing the cursor to be a hand when hovering over these buttons would make the user interface more cohesive and could allow for more users to utilize the multiple-month viewing feature.

```text
1	# Example: Browser-driven web app
2	
3	You have a dev server that serves HTML to a browser. An agent in a
4	headless container can't open a browser window - so "run the app" means
5	launching the dev server, driving a headless Chromium against it, and
6	producing a screenshot that proves the page rendered.
7	
8	Don't write a browser driver. Use `chromium-cli`.
9	
10	## Dev server
11	
12	Find the dev command (`package.json` `scripts.dev`, `Makefile`,
13	README), start it in the background, and wait for it to actually serve:
14	
15	```bash
16	npm run dev &   # or yarn dev, pnpm dev, make serve, ./dev.sh
17	timeout 30 bash -c 'until curl -sf http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
18	```
19	
20	Don't `sleep 5` - poll the port. Stop by killing the port's listener
21	-- `lsof -ti:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs -r kill` - before relaunching,
22	or the next run hits `EADDRINUSE`. (`$!` after `npm run dev &` is only
23	the npm wrapper; npm doesn't forward SIGTERM to the server it spawned,
24	so the port kill is what actually frees it.) Avoid `pkill -f` with a
25	broad pattern - it can match the agent's own command line and kill the
26	session.
27	
28	## Drive
29	
30	`chromium-cli` is a headless-Chromium REPL. Pipe a script to stdin:
31	
32	```bash
33	chromium-cli --session app <<'EOF'
34	nav http://localhost:3000
35	wait-for text=Dashboard
36	screenshot
37	click button:has-text("New item")
38	fill input[name="title"] Smoke test
39	press Enter
40	wait-for text=Smoke test
41	screenshot
42	console --errors
43	EOF
44	```
45	
46	Screenshots land in `chromium_cli/sessions/app/screenshots/` (latest
47	symlinked as `screenshot.png`). That's the whole loop: `nav` ->
48	`wait-for` the element you need -> act (`click` / `fill` / `type` /
49	`press`) -> `screenshot` -> `console --errors` to check nothing threw.
50	Full command reference: `chromium-cli` skill, or `help` at the prompt.
51	
52	For iterative debugging, run it under tmux and `send-keys` one command
53	at a time - same commands, same session.
54	
55	**If `chromium-cli` isn't available:** adapt
56	[electron.md](electron.md)'s REPL driver - the structure and commands
57	transfer, but it's `_electron`-specific:
58	import `{ chromium }` instead, launch with
59	`chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox'] })`, acquire the page via
60	`(await app.newContext()).newPage()` then `goto()` your dev URL, and
61	drop the Electron-only window introspection
62	(`.windows()`/`.firstWindow()`/the `windows` command).
63	
64	## What to put in the skill
65	
66	The project-specific bits only. `chromium-cli` handles the mechanics.
67	
68	- **Dev command + port + stop.** The exact start line, any env vars it
69	  needs, and the `kill` to stop it.
70	- **Auth.** Whatever gets a logged-in session - a `set-cookie` line, a
71	  `fill`/`click` login sequence, or a helper script that does the API
72	  dance and emits the cookie.
73	- **One representative interaction.** Not the whole app - one path that
74	  proves it's running, ending in a screenshot.
75	- **App-specific gotchas.** Only the ones you actually hit.
76	
77	## Gotchas that recur
78	
79	- **React controlled inputs.** `eval el.value = '...'` doesn't fire
80	  React's onChange. Use `fill` / `type` - they go through Playwright's
81	  input pipeline.
82	- **Websockets / long-poll.** `wait-idle` never settles. `wait-for` the
83	  element you actually need.
84	- **Slow first paint.** Vite/Next compile routes on demand; the first
85	  `nav` can take 10s+. `wait-for` handles it; raw `sleep` doesn't.
86	- **`screenshot-element <sel>`** crops to one element - use it when the
87	  diff is in a specific component, not the whole page.
88	- **Check `console --errors` before declaring success.** A page can
89	  render its shell while every data fetch 500s.
90

const { chromium } = require('playwright');

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1400, height: 900 } });
  const logs = [];
  page.on('console', msg => logs.push(`[${msg.type()}] ${msg.text()}`));
  page.on('pageerror', err => logs.push(`[pageerror] ${err.message}`));

  await page.goto('http://localhost:3001', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded', timeout: 30000 });
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  await page.screenshot({ path: 'C:/Users/Kirby/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Actual-Budget/5fdb5449-4529-4a70-a8d1-a2c36e8bb7cd/scratchpad/00-initial.png' });

  console.log('URL:', page.url());
  console.log('Title:', await page.title());
  console.log('--- body text sample ---');
  console.log((await page.locator('body').innerText()).slice(0, 800));
  console.log('--- console/page logs ---');
  console.log(logs.join('\n'));

  await browser.close();
})();

```

const { chromium } = require('playwright');

const shot = name =>

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1400, height: 900 } });
  page.on('pageerror', err => console.log('[pageerror]', err.message));

  await page.goto('http://localhost:3001', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded', timeout: 30000 });

  const dontUseServer = page.getByText("Don't use a server", { exact: false });
  if (await dontUseServer.isVisible({ timeout: 10000 }).catch(() => false)) {
    await dontUseServer.click();
  }

  await page.waitForTimeout(1000);
  await page.screenshot({ path: shot('01-setup') });

  const viewDemo = page.getByText('View demo', { exact: false });
  if (await viewDemo.isVisible({ timeout: 10000 }).catch(() => false)) {
    await viewDemo.click();
  }

  await page.waitForURL('**/budget**', { timeout: 20000 }).catch(() => {});
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  console.log('URL after demo click:', page.url());
  await page.screenshot({ path: shot('02-budget-page') });

  const icons = page.locator('svg').filter({ hasText: '' });
  console.log('body sample:', (await page.locator('body').innerText()).slice(0, 300));

  await browser.close();
})();

  await page.goto('http://localhost:3001', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
  const dontUseServer = page.getByText(\"Don't use a server\", { exact: false });
  await dontUseServer.click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  const viewDemo = page.getByText('View demo', { exact: false });
  await viewDemo.waitFor({ timeout: 15000 });
  await viewDemo.click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/budget**', { timeout: 20000 }).catch(() => {});
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);

  const buttons = await page.\$\$('[title=\"Choose the number of months shown at a time\"] button');
  console.log('found buttons:', buttons.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < buttons.length; i++) {
    const btn = buttons[i];
    const box = await btn.boundingBox();
    await page.mouse.move(box.x + box.width/2, box.y + box.height/2);
    await page.waitForTimeout(300);
    const cursor = await btn.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).cursor);
    const bg = await btn.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor);
    console.log('Icon', i+1, 'cursor=', cursor, 'bg=', bg);
    await page.screenshot({ path: shot('hover-mc-' + (i+1)), clip: { x: 240, y: 0, width: 120, height: 40 } });
  }

  // move mouse away, baseline screenshot
  await page.mouse.move(700, 400);
  await page.waitForTimeout(200);
  await page.screenshot({ path: shot('hover-mc-none'), clip: { x: 240, y: 0, width: 120, height: 40 } });

  // Today button
  const todayIconEl = await page.\$('[title=\"Today\"]');
  const todayBtn = await todayIconEl.evaluateHandle(el => el.closest('button'));
  const todayBtnEl = todayBtn.asElement();
  const box2 = await todayBtnEl.boundingBox();
  await page.mouse.move(box2.x + box2.width/2, box2.y + box2.height/2);
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  const cursor2 = await todayBtnEl.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).cursor);
  const bg2 = await todayBtnEl.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor);
  console.log('Today cursor=', cursor2, 'bg=', bg2);
  await page.screenshot({ path: shot('hover-today'), clip: { x: 600, y: 20, width: 150, height: 60 } });

  await browser.close();
})();
"

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
3	
4	import { SvgCalendar } from '@actual-app/components/icons/v2';
5	import { theme } from '@actual-app/components/theme';
6	import { View } from '@actual-app/components/view';
7	
8	import { Link } from '#components/common/Link';
9	
10	import { useBudgetMonthCount } from './BudgetMonthCountContext';
11	
12	type CalendarProps = {
13	  color: string;
14	  onClick: () => void;
15	};
16	
17	function Calendar({ color, onClick }: CalendarProps) {
18	  return (
19	    <Link
20	      variant="button"
21	      buttonVariant="bare"
22	      onPress={onClick}
23	      style={{ padding: 2, marginRight: 3 }}
24	    >
25	      <SvgCalendar style={{ width: 13, height: 13, color }} />
26	    </Link>
27	  );
28	}
29	
30	type MonthCountSelectorProps = {
31	  maxMonths: number;
32	  onChange: (value: number) => void;
33	};
34	
35	export function MonthCountSelector({
36	  maxMonths,
37	  onChange,
38	}: MonthCountSelectorProps) {
39	  const { t } = useTranslation();
40	
41	  const { displayMax } = useBudgetMonthCount();
42	
43	  // It doesn't make sense to show anything if we can only fit one
44	  // month
45	  if (displayMax <= 1) {
46	    return null;
47	  }
48	
49	  const calendars = [];
50	  for (let i = 1; i <= displayMax; i++) {
51	    calendars.push(
52	      <Calendar
53	        key={i}
54	        color={maxMonths >= i ? theme.pageTextLight : theme.pageTextSubdued}
55	        onClick={() => onChange(i)}
56	      />,
57	    );
58	  }
59	
60	  return (
61	    <View
62	      style={{
63	        flexDirection: 'row',
64	        marginRight: 20,
65	        marginTop: -1,
66	        WebkitAppRegion: 'no-drag',
67	        '& svg': {
68	          transition: 'transform .15s',
69	        },
70	        '& svg:hover': {
71	          transform: 'scale(1.2)',
72	        },
73	      }}
74	      title={t('Choose the number of months shown at a time')}
75	    >
76	      {calendars}
77	    </View>
78	  );
79	}

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-11 01:10:31Z)**_

No test file in the codebase mocks react-i18next — `useTranslation()`'s `t` works untouched via i18next's default passthrough (returns the key/string as-is), so `t('Choose the number of months shown at a time')` needs no mock. I have enough to write the report.

## Findings

**Best examples found** (all under `packages/desktop-client/src/components/`):

1. **`common/CalculatorButtons.test.tsx`** — best match for MonthCountSelector: small, no-context component, tests click handlers via `fireEvent.click`.
2. **`accounts/Balance.test.tsx`** (`SelectedBalance`) — shows `vi.mock('#hooks/...')` pattern and `TestProviders` wrapper, `vi.clearAllMocks()` in `beforeEach`.
3. **`reports/Change.test.tsx`** — simplest `TestProviders`-wrapped component test, minimal boilerplate.

### Import/header boilerplate (consistent across all three)
```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { render, screen, fireEvent } from '@testing-library/react'; // fireEvent only where needed
import { TestProviders } from '#mocks';          // only when redux/query context needed
import { ComponentUnderTest } from './Component';
```
No file-level "use client" or license header. `describe`/`it` (or `test`) are globals (vitest globals enabled), no explicit import of `describe/it/expect/vi` needed — confirmed `Balance.test.tsx` uses `vi.mock`/`vi.mocked` and `beforeEach` with no import statement for them (global vitest API).

### Representative test (CalculatorButtons — closest analog, no context)
```tsx
describe('CalculatorButtons', () => {
  it('updates a controlled external input from keypad actions', () => {
    render(<TestCalculator />);
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: '1' }));
    expect(input).toHaveValue('12+3');
  });
});
```

### Context/hooks
`TestProviders` (`packages/desktop-client/src/mocks.tsx`) wraps only Redux `Provider` + `QueryClientProvider` — it does **not** cover `BudgetMonthCountContext`. For `MonthCountSelector`, the real `BudgetMonthCountProvider` (`./BudgetMonthCountContext.tsx`) should be used directly as a wrapper (it's a simple `useState`-backed provider, no external deps), e.g. `render(<BudgetMonthCountProvider><MonthCountSelector .../></BudgetMonthCountProvider>)`. Alternatively `vi.mock('./BudgetMonthCountContext', () => ({ useBudgetMonthCount: () => ({ displayMax: 3 }) }))` mirrors the `vi.mock('#hooks/...')` pattern seen in `Balance.test.tsx`/`GoCardlessExternalMsgModal.test.tsx` — either is idiomatic; mocking is more common when the hook is imported from a `#hooks/*` alias.

### i18n
No test file mocks `react-i18next`. `useTranslation()`'s `t()` is used unmocked and just returns the key/string passed in — no i18n provider or mock needed for tests that only assert on rendered text/attributes.

### Click/mouse interaction
`CalculatorButtons.test.tsx` uses `fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: ... }))` throughout — no `userEvent` usage was found in the sampled files, and no hover-specific tests were found; click via `fireEvent` is the established pattern for button-role elements (matches MonthCountSelector's `Link`/`onPress` calendar buttons, which render as clickable elements).

### No custom `render()` helper
There is no wrapping custom `render` (like `renderWithProviders`); tests call `@testing-library/react`'s `render` directly, wrapping children in `<TestProviders>` only when redux/query-client context is actually needed (not needed for MonthCountSelector beyond the budget-month-count context).

1	import { useCallback } from 'react';
2	import {
3	  useLocation,
4	  // oxlint-disable-next-line eslint/no-restricted-imports
5	  useNavigate as useNavigateReactRouter,
6	} from 'react-router';
7	import type {
8	  Location,
9	  NavigateFunction,
10	  NavigateOptions,
11	  To,
12	} from 'react-router';
13	
14	export function useNavigate(): NavigateFunction {
15	  const location = useLocation();
16	  const navigate = useNavigateReactRouter();
17	  return useCallback(
18	    (to: To | number, options: NavigateOptions = {}) => {
19	      if (typeof to === 'number') {
20	        void navigate(to);
21	      } else {
22	        const optionsWithPrevLocation: NavigateOptions = {
23	          replace:
24	            options.replace || isSamePath(to, location) ? true : undefined,
25	          ...options,
26	          state: {
27	            ...options?.state,
28	            previousLocation: location,
29	          },
30	        };
31	
32	        const { previousLocation, ...previousOriginalState } =
33	          location.state || {};
34	
35	        if (
36	          previousLocation == null ||
37	          !isSamePath(to, previousLocation) ||
38	          JSON.stringify(options?.state || {}) !==
39	            JSON.stringify(previousOriginalState)
40	        ) {
41	          void navigate(to, optionsWithPrevLocation);
42	        } else {
43	          // `to` is the same as the previous location. Just go back.
44	          void navigate(-1);
45	        }
46	      }
47	    },
48	    [navigate, location],
49	  );
50	}
51	
52	function isSamePath(to: To, location: Location) {
53	  return to === location.pathname + location.search + location.hash;
54	}
55

import React from 'react';

import { render, screen, fireEvent } from '@testing-library/react';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router';

import { useBudgetMonthCount } from './BudgetMonthCountContext';
import { MonthCountSelector } from './MonthCountSelector';

vi.mock('./BudgetMonthCountContext', () => ({
  useBudgetMonthCount: vi.fn(),
}));

function renderSelector(maxMonths: number, onChange: (value: number) => void) {
  return render(
    <MemoryRouter>
      <MonthCountSelector maxMonths={maxMonths} onChange={onChange} />
    </MemoryRouter>,
  );
}

describe('MonthCountSelector', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
  });

  test('renders nothing when only one month fits on screen', () => {
    vi.mocked(useBudgetMonthCount).mockReturnValue({
      displayMax: 1,
      setDisplayMax: vi.fn(),
    });

    const { container } = renderSelector(1, vi.fn());

    expect(container).toBeEmptyDOMElement();
  });

  test('renders one calendar button per month that can be displayed', () => {
    vi.mocked(useBudgetMonthCount).mockReturnValue({
      displayMax: 3,
      setDisplayMax: vi.fn(),
    });

    renderSelector(2, vi.fn());

    const buttons = screen.getAllByRole('button');
    expect(buttons).toHaveLength(3);
    // Each icon is a real, focusable button so it picks up the app's
    // standard pointer-cursor/hover-background button styling.
    for (const button of buttons) {
      expect(button.tagName).toBe('BUTTON');
    }
  });

  test('calls onChange with the 1-based index of the clicked month', () => {
    vi.mocked(useBudgetMonthCount).mockReturnValue({
      displayMax: 3,
      setDisplayMax: vi.fn(),
    });
    const onChange = vi.fn();

    renderSelector(1, onChange);

    const buttons = screen.getAllByRole('button');
    fireEvent.click(buttons[2]);

    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith(3);
  });

  test('highlights months up to maxMonths and dims the rest', () => {
    vi.mocked(useBudgetMonthCount).mockReturnValue({
      displayMax: 3,
      setDisplayMax: vi.fn(),
    });

    renderSelector(2, vi.fn());

    const icons = screen
      .getAllByRole('button')
      .map(button => button.querySelector('svg'));

    expect(icons[0]).toHaveStyle({ color: 'var(--color-pageTextLight)' });
    expect(icons[1]).toHaveStyle({ color: 'var(--color-pageTextLight)' });
    expect(icons[2]).toHaveStyle({ color: 'var(--color-pageTextSubdued)' });
  });
});

```

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`
